routes.label: Add one and use common divisors

question:
Four positive integers \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) have a product of \(8!\) and satisfy

\[ab + a + b = 524,\]\[bc + b + c = 146,\]\[cd + c + d = 104.\]

What is \(a - d?\)
solution:
Each expression has the form \(uv+u+v\), which becomes a product after adding \(1\):
\[
uv+u+v+1=u(v+1)+(v+1)=(u+1)(v+1).
\]
The three equations therefore become
\[
(a+1)(b+1)=525,
\]
\[
(b+1)(c+1)=147,
\]
\[
(c+1)(d+1)=105.
\]
This makes the integer restrictions useful. Set \(t=b+1\). Since \(b\) is positive, \(t\ge2\). The first two products show that \(t\) divides both \(525\) and \(147\), whose greatest common factor is \(21\). Thus
\[
t\in\{3,7,21\}.
\]
These three cases exhaust the possibilities.

If \(t=3\), then \(c+1=147/3=49\). But \(49\) does not divide \(105\), so the third equation cannot give an integer \(d\).

If \(t=7\), the three products give
\[
(a,b,c,d)=(74,6,20,4).
\]
Its product is \(74\cdot6\cdot20\cdot4=35520\), so it fails the factorial condition.

If \(t=21\), they give
\[
(a,b,c,d)=(24,20,6,14).
\]
All four integers are positive, and their product is
\[
24\cdot20\cdot6\cdot14=40320=8!.
\]
The factorizations were reversible, so this tuple also satisfies all three original equations. Therefore \(\boxed{a-d=24-14=10}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
